goal_en: Ask questions with W-words and understand train times.

scene.setting_en: Emma wants to go to Freising to see the hospital. She asks Herr Maier at the station.

lines.speaker: emma
lines.de: Entschuldigung, wann fährt die S-Bahn nach Freising?
lines.en: Excuse me, when does the S-Bahn to Freising leave?

lines.speaker: herr_maier
lines.de: Die nächste S-Bahn fährt um neun Uhr.
lines.en: The next S-Bahn leaves at nine o'clock.

lines.speaker: emma
lines.de: Und wo kaufe ich eine Fahrkarte?
lines.en: And where do I buy a ticket?

lines.speaker: herr_maier
lines.en: You're welcome. Have a good trip!

vocabulary.example_de: Der Zug fährt von Gleis eins.
vocabulary.example_en: The train leaves from platform one.

vocabulary.en: to go / to drive / to leave (vehicles)
vocabulary.example_de: Die S-Bahn fährt um neun Uhr.

vocabulary.example_en: Where do I buy a ticket?
Excuse me, where is platform two?
Thank you very much, Mr Maier!

grammar.explanation_en: Most German question words start with W: wer (who), was (what), wo (where), wann (when), woher (where from), wie (how). In a W-question, the verb comes in second position, right after the question word: 'Wann fährt die S-Bahn?'. Some verbs change their vowel with du, er, sie: 'ich fahre' but 'die S-Bahn fährt'.

examples.de: Wann fährt die S-Bahn nach Freising?
examples.en: When does the S-Bahn to Freising leave?
Where do I buy a ticket?

exercises.translation_en: Where is the machine? – Over there.

exercises.prompt_en: Put the words in the right order.
Listen and type the platform number as a digit.
exercises.text_de: Die S-Bahn fährt von Gleis drei.
exercises.translation_en: The S-Bahn leaves from platform three.

exercises.prompt_en: Match the German and English words.

dialogue.setting_en: You want to go to Munich. At the station you meet Frau Huber.

turns.speaker: frau_huber
turns.de: Oh, hallo Emma! Wohin fahren Sie?
turns.en: Oh, hello Emma! Where are you going?

options.feedback_en: 'aus' means 'from'. Use 'nach' for where you are going.
The order is mixed up: 'Ich fahre nach München.'

turns.speaker: frau_huber
turns.de: Schön! Haben Sie schon eine Fahrkarte?
turns.en: Nice! Do you already have a ticket?

options.feedback_en: 'wann' asks about time. For a place, use 'wo'.
In a question the verb comes second: 'Wo ist der Automat?'

turns.speaker: frau_huber
turns.de: Da drüben, neben Gleis eins. Gute Fahrt!
turns.en: Over there, next to platform one. Have a good trip!
